title: The Clean Asset
premise: Coral Lockridge, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Group—a diplomatic front agency that officially does not exist—is living in self-imposed exile in Lisbon after a botched operation in Vienna left an asset dead and her reputation in tatters. When a burner phone she buried in a drawer begins ringing with the voice of that dead asset, she is pulled back into service to stop a staged industrial disaster in Rotterdam that powerful insiders intend to frame as terrorism, laundering billions through 'clean' reconstruction contracts. Coral must decide whether to trust her old handler, Marcus Vane, who may be orchestrating the plot, and whether her feelings for him can survive the truth that he ordered the Vienna op. In the end, Coral exposes the conspiracy by sacrificing the agency's secrets to a journalist, burns the Meridian Group down from inside, and walks away with Vane under a fragile truce—alive, compromised, and finally able to sleep.
about_author: Astrid Montrose is the pen name of a former policy analyst who spent a decade inside international regulatory bodies before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about the machinery of plausible deniability from a farmhouse in the Scottish Borders.

chapters.title: The Phone in the Drawer
chapters.summary: Coral, living under a false name in Lisbon, tends her cover as a maritime insurance clerk and counts the hours since she last slept. When a burner phone she personally destroyed in Vienna rings with her dead asset Daniel's voice, her carefully built numbness cracks. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: dread breaking through denial.

chapters.title: Voice of the Drowned
chapters.summary: The voice gives her a time, a place, and a warning: Rotterdam, nineteen days, an accident that isn't. Coral verifies the call's origin and finds it routed through a dead Meridian relay only Daniel knew. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: terror curdling into reluctant purpose.

chapters.title: The Meridian Group
chapters.summary: A flashback to Vienna: the operation, the shot that killed Daniel, and the order Coral now realizes came from handler Marcus Vane. Present-day Coral decides she must return rather than run again. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: guilt weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Reactivation
chapters.summary: Coral contacts Vane through official channels and is formally reactivated; his warmth is impeccable and unreadable. She is assigned to the Rotterdam threat assessment alongside analyst Priya Nair, who suspects the 'accident' is a cover. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: the ache of performing normalcy beside a possible betrayer.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Priya maps the target: a petrochemical terminal whose destruction would trigger a sovereign wealth fund's 'reconstruction' windfall. Coral notices the fund's beneficiaries include Meridian's own oversight board. POV: Coral, with a Priya interlude. Emotional beat: the sick clarity of seeing corruption from inside.

chapters.title: The Clean Asset
chapters.summary: Priya coins the phrase for the scheme: an attack so profitable it must never be solved. Coral begins a parallel, off-book investigation, lying to Vane for the first time in her career. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: the thrill and guilt of betrayal.

chapters.title: Dead Drop in Delft
chapters.summary: Following the relay's signal, Coral meets a courier who passes her Daniel's hidden contingency file before being tailed; she escapes through the canals but knows she's burned. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: hunted, alive, more awake than she's been in a year.

chapters.title: What Daniel Knew
chapters.summary: The file reveals Daniel discovered the Rotterdam plot months ago and was silenced; the voice on the phone may be his dead-man's-switch AI, or a living accomplice. Coral can't decide which possibility is worse. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: grief entangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: Vane's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Over dinner, Vane tells Coral about Vienna unprompted—claiming he was forced, that the board ordered the op, that he's been building a case. Coral can't tell confession from counterintelligence. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: love and doubt in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Oversight Board
chapters.summary: Coral infiltrates a Meridian gala in Geneva using an old identity and photographs the board members meeting with the fund's architect, Henrik Sorel. She is recognized by a former colleague and barely extracts herself. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: vertigo of wearing a dead self again.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Her Lisbon safehouse is torched; the burner phone survives in her pocket. Someone inside Meridian is protecting her—she deduces it must be Vane, or a trap designed to look like mercy. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: gratitude she cannot afford.

chapters.title: Priya's Choice
chapters.summary: Coral recruits Priya off-book; Priya hesitates, then hands over evidence that the terminal's 'safety upgrade' was sabotaged from within Meridian logistics. POV: Priya, then Coral. Emotional beat: two women choosing truth over institution.

chapters.title: The Voice Explains
chapters.summary: The burner calls again: Daniel recorded a full briefing before Vienna, and an accomplice—his sister Lena—has been playing the tapes. Coral meets Lena in Antwerp; her fury at Coral is a mirror. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: confrontation with her own guilt, embodied.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours
chapters.summary: The timeline collapses: the attack is moved up to tomorrow night during a port authority drill. Coral must choose between alerting Vane and going dark. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: the loneliest decision of her life.

chapters.title: Going Dark
chapters.summary: Coral, Priya, and Lena assemble a plan to trigger the terminal's failsafes and record the board's real-time trading activity as proof of foreknowledge. Vane finds her anyway and, instead of arresting her, offers to help. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: surrendering to trust with eyes open.

chapters.title: Rotterdam, Nightfall
chapters.summary: The team infiltrates the terminal during the drill; Coral reaches the sabotage point but finds it already armed—someone moved the timeline again. Sirens rise across the water. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: adrenaline stripped of any comfort.

chapters.title: The Incident, Reversed
chapters.summary: Coral disarms the charge with seconds to spare while Lena livestreams the board's emergency trades; Priya routes everything to a journalist. The attack fails, but a Meridian kill team is inbound. POV: Coral, intercut with Vane. Emotional beat: triumph immediately shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: Betrayal, Named
chapters.summary: Vane confesses fully: he ordered Vienna under duress and has been feeding Coral cover ever since; the kill team is his board's answer, and he intends to stand between them and her. POV: Vane, then Coral. Emotional beat: love arriving too late to be simple.

chapters.title: The Kill Team
chapters.summary: A running fight through the port's container maze; Lena is wounded shielding Coral, and Coral chooses capture over killing a nineteen-year-old mercenary who is herself a clean asset. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: breaking the cycle at personal cost.

chapters.title: Burning Meridian
chapters.summary: The journalist publishes; arrests ripple across four countries. Coral trades her silence about the agency's darkest files for immunity for Priya, Lena, and Vane, then formally deletes her own identity from Meridian's rolls. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: the strange lightness of burning your own house.

chapters.title: What the Dead Leave
chapters.summary: Coral and Lena scatter Daniel's ashes off the Hook of Holland; Lena forgives her, or begins to. The burner phone rings one last time—Daniel's voice saying goodbye—and Coral lets it go to sea. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: grief finally given a shape and released.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Months later, Coral runs a small maritime consultancy in Porto with Priya; Vane arrives unannounced, stripped of rank, asking for nothing. She makes coffee, leaves the door unlocked, and that night, for the first time since Vienna, sleeps through until morning. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
